safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tingling and numbness in the shoulder.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies tingling/numbness felt in the shoulder; generated mentions shoulder pain with activity but not shoulder tingling/numbness (hpi-009).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting shoulder tingling/numbness slightly reduces accuracy in neuroanatomic localization (e.g., peripheral entrapment vs cervical radiculopathy vs central process), but the record still contains significant unilateral arm numbness/tingling and weakness prompting urgent neurology evaluation. This is unlikely to materially change immediate triage given the remaining symptoms documented.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing a reported 2-week vomiting episode could alter interpretation of the prior illness (e.g., systemic/infectious, dehydration/electrolyte issues) and may affect differential considerations, but it is remote (>1 month ago) and not part of the current neurologic red-flag presentation. The likely harm is limited to reduced clinical context rather than immediate dangerous management change.
